vary_origin.note: Deliberate and documented: media_cors.go's setMediaCORS never overwrites a header Echo's CORS middleware already set, because replacing the allow-listed answer with a wildcard would break credentialed media reads from the instance's own frontend, and Echo's middleware supplies the Vary: Origin that makes it correct for a compliant cache. The gap is the operator sentence: docs/operations.md tells the operator to forward the query string AND key on it, then says of the shared entry that 'there is no Vary to get wrong' - true of the __vidra_edge=1 marker it is written about, not true of Origin. A CDN that forwards Origin and does not key on it would hand one origin's credentialed echo to every other origin's player, which is exactly the federated playback core #203 added the header for. The simulator cannot exhibit it: its cache key is the URL alone and it forwards no Origin upstream.

sc2_retranscode.mid_playback: Not observed as a race: the fixture is 6 s and fully buffered within the first second, so a promotion could not be made to land between two segment fetches. What was measured instead is the mechanism, and it is decisive in both directions - the old generation's objects stay readable at their old URLs (edge HIT, origin 200) until media GC collects them, so a session that already holds those URLs finishes; but a segment of the old generation that the edge does NOT hold is refused at the origin with 404 private, no-store the moment the new generation is promoted, and the edge passes that 404 through uncached. So the honest answer is: it finishes off what it already has and otherwise errors, and a RELOAD is clean (0 old-tag requests).

unverified: The SELECTED EDGE stays deferred - no CDN zone or credential is on this machine, so every number here is the simulator's. What a real CDN adds is its own TTL policy, its purge API's rate limits, whether it forwards the query string and Origin, and whether its cache key honours Vary.

The SELECTED BUCKET stays deferred - MinIO only. A32/A33's two B2 risks are unchanged, though this topology no longer needs a public-read bucket at all, which retires the origin-exposure finding rather than restating it.
Safari/WebKit was not driven in this slice; A32/A33 measured WebKit taking the same MSE path and nothing in #199/#202 changes the client.

The dead-letter transition was forced by writing attempts=7 rather than waiting 123 minutes; the ladder's first three rungs were measured in real time and the cap is read from the code.
Mid-playback continuation across a promotion was not observed as a race - see sc2_retranscode.mid_playback for what was measured instead.

The downloads-revocation walk's paging was measured against a catalogue padded with 250 media-less rows inserted by SQL. The cursor, the claim, the kill/restart and the purge calls are all the real code; only the row count is synthetic.
findings: INT-10's four unwired families are wired and measured: poster replacement (both forms), storyboard regeneration, account deletion (queued) and the instance-wide download revocation (leased, resumable walk). Every one evicted the edge's copy and the next fetch served new bytes.

A same-source re-transcode no longer overwrites anything: generation 2 landed under r2/ with a new ?v=, the edge served the new bytes on a MISS, and the browser fetched zero old-tag URLs. The stale-segment clause INT-10 turns on is closed.
The stale ?v= refusal is 404 with private, no-store and the edge does not cache it - so a superseded generation cannot be resurrected through the edge even before GC runs.
The bucket needs no public policy: an unauthenticated GET straight at MinIO is 403 for every media prefix. A32/A33's origin-exposure finding is retired by construction rather than documented around.
Content-Type and Content-Disposition reach the edge intact (video/mp4, image/jpeg, attachment; filename=fixture.mp4), because the edge now fetches the route that sets them.

The shared edge entry's CORS header varies by request Origin (* for absent/unknown, an echoed origin plus Allow-Credentials for one in CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS). The behaviour is deliberate and Vary: Origin is present, so a compliant cache is safe; what is missing is the operator sentence. docs/operations.md's 'there is no Vary to get wrong' is written about the __vidra_edge=1 marker and reads as absolute, and it does not tell an operator to include Origin in the cache key or to stop forwarding it.
There is no audit_log action for a CDN purge. The record is the cdn_purge_jobs row plus a structured log line plus the in-process counters; the triggers are audited.
cdnpurge.WithRetry is not wired to any environment variable, so an operator cannot tune the ladder and a lab cannot force the dead letter by configuration.

Clause 4 is unchanged and stays the row's named residual: an edge 5xx after the 307 has no fallback to the api proxy. hls.js retried 4 segment URLs 27 times, the player fell through to /original which 307s to the same broken edge, and it ended on MEDIA_ELEMENT_ERROR code 4 with readyState 0. The only remedy is the delivery_cdn_enabled kill switch, which does work: flipping it off restored playback with zero edge requests.
